analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing
key_insights: Post-election session (Nov 5, 2026): SPX +0.1%, NDX -0.5%, RTY +0.4% pre-market. WTI $88.54, gold $4,124, 10Y 4.878%, VIX 16.83. Desk flags a continued rotation and Momentum unwind, with Semis and Memory selling off.

Equity derivatives desk (Christina Jones) reads the breadth expansion as positioning-driven, not a fundamental rotation. Customers are buying short-dated calls in popular shorts as hedges but not chasing laggards. Conviction is low and flows are orderly. The only true rotation is within TMT, toward large-cap quality with financing access and compute ownership.

Clients said they want five conditions before re-risking into AI: midterms passed, capex guidance reiterated, Semis earnings, a positioning washout, and reopened AI capital markets. Most are met, but the Democratic sweep adds regulatory headwinds that are triggering a lower rerating of the group.
APAC clients expect AI capex cuts could come as soon as early 2027 on revenue headwinds. The election timing may accelerate that view.

Momentum had a second -6z move in a week after the hyperscaler selloff, and -5.8z is the largest single-month underperformance in more than 40 years (Arun Jain). Both long and short legs lost. Momentum Crowding had its second largest decline since the GFC, with positioning at the 47th percentile on a 5-year lookback.
The Anti-AI vs Broadening trade has been unwinding for weeks. A Middle East resolution, which the desk calls a clear Democratic priority, would add a tailwind to broadening.

International Market Intel (Fede and Victoria): the market reads the Democratic sweep as a flatter Iran geopolitical risk curve, constraints on data centers and more fiscal discipline. All three are positive for rates. The global oil balance is back in surplus at 1.4 mbd in October vs ~1.3 mbd on average last year.

Semis analyst Gokul Hariharan is bullish. Unit economics are the best this cycle, AI scaling laws are intact, token demand has recovered, compute pricing is strong, hyperscaler capex intent is rising, and classic cycle-peak signs are absent. Risks are neocloud funding concerns, compute price ($/W) compression, and datacenter buildout impediments.

JPM Credit: slowing data center development is not necessarily bad. No material change is expected to 2027 capital plans, but there could be an impact in 2028 and beyond. Bond supply is expected to slow near-term, with the first new deals focused on data centers and GPUs in 'safe' jurisdictions.

JPM Credit: about 45 local ballot measures across 13 states restrict data centers. IPPs with exposure in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia are expected to be weak. Behind-the-meter bridge power providers face the largest near-term negative impact. About 27% of MW of data center capacity funded in the HY project finance market is being built in Texas.

Positioning Intelligence: WTI positioning rose from +0.4z to +0.9z with 77% of clients net long (94th percentile over 12m). US gas net positioning fell from -0.5z to -3.4z on Monday, the lowest since 2021, then -2.9z after Tuesday's covering. The oil vs gas gap hit a record 4.1z. A gas bounce is more likely than not but history suggests only about +4%.

Positioning Intelligence: NDX futures positioning is still +1.3z (93rd percentile) despite a 20-day decline, which may limit the NDX bounce versus RTY. T-Bond positioning shifted from covering to buying (1-week +1.2z). Copper is at -2z and gold positioning is below its long-term average.

Nikos: October hedge fund de-risking and AI liquidations create a more favorable year-end backdrop. Retail buying of equity funds could stabilize AI stocks in November, with hedge funds rebuilding AI exposure from end-November. Real-money long-duration investors could limit further yield declines. The Binance hack exposed infrastructure risk but crypto stayed resilient.

Trading desk (Ron Adler): the election is behind us and the VIX reflects relief. Flows have a modest +SPX/-RTY tilt but demand turned more defensive through the morning. The margin of victory was more surprising than the result.
TMT desk (Mark Schilsky): Internet outperformed Software (KWEB +5% vs IGV +1%). EXPE +12%, BKNG +11%, APP +10%, RDDT +8%, ETSY +8%, WIX +6%.
Consumer desk (Alex Murphy): consumer price action is better than sponsorship. Discretionary demand is mostly hedge fund short covering. Genuine long demand is narrow, in LTH, DAL, WYNN and KDP.

Rates desk (Alexa Hanelin): USTs are 2-4bp richer with the curve bull steepening. Quarterly Refunding is at 8:30am, and JPM expects unchanged coupon sizes with next week's 3s/10s/30s at $58bn/$42bn/$25bn. The risk is skewed toward cuts in longer-dated sizes. Strategy remains in 10s30s steepeners.

US Market Intel View: JPM sticks with its Tactically Bullish call. When NDX is within ~6% of its ATH and falls 3.5%+, it rebounds ~3% the following week on average, with a stronger effect after a Friday decline.

JPM argues AI capex declines would not trigger a recession. Reasons: record household net worth, strong cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI not being a significant hiring driver. CRWV employs only about 550 people. The main effect would be lower capex and possible hyperscaler layoffs.

Biggest non-AI risk is Middle East re-escalation. Oil appears to have priced another attack, which limits upside for energy, yields and equity downside. Positive November and post-midterm seasonality return.

Monetization Menu (Nov 2): broadening can continue via a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals. Consumers and Financials can work if the curve steepens. Europe could catch a bid if US/Iran move toward a deal. In Jan-Feb, US Value was +7.4%, SXXP +7.6% and UKX +9.7%.

Semis analyst Gokul Hariharan says the set-up is anticipating an EPS cut soon, so continued EPS revisions could drive markets up. This is an expectation, not a print.
Ron Adler says earnings season has been solid, with no specific figures given.

The global oil balance is back in surplus versus ~1.3 mbd on average last year, which could ease pressure on central banks.
Yields fell on the election outcome, and JPM Strategy sees constraint on fiscal expansion.
JPM expects the refunding to leave sizes unchanged. The risk is toward cuts in longer-dated sizes. An unchanged announcement could steepen the curve if the market priced something more activist.

tension_points.bull_case: Companies with existing deals, capacity or projects underway benefit, hyperscalers are net positive, semis fundamentals are strong and the set-up already anticipates an EPS cut (Hariharan, Adler).
tension_points.bear_case: Investors see regulatory headwinds from the Democratic sweep triggering a lower rerating, with possible capex cuts as early as early 2027 and a bottom hard to see ahead of capital markets events.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex cuts arriving as soon as early 2027, or capital markets for AI not reopening for 2028 and beyond projects.

tension_points.bull_case: Consumer outperformance and robust household balance sheets support spending.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary demand is mainly hedge fund short covering and genuine long demand is narrow, so the rally is factor driven (Alex Murphy).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broader evidence of real-money participation in Consumer would change the bearish read.

tension_points.bull_case: Democratic control checks fiscal expansion, and AI-related and UST issuance should lower long-end term premia.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor data are firm, services inflation is elevated and ISM services is expected around 55-55.5, so the backdrop does not call for much lower yields. Real-money duration investors may cap declines.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An unchanged refunding announcement could steepen the curve if the market priced something more activist.
